Loss-of-function mutations in OFD1 disrupt the normal functioning of ciliogenesis and centrosome organization. partners.mechanism_chain: OFD1 (HGNC:8670) —DISRUPTS→ centrosome function and ciliogenesis (GO:0034343|GO:0005813); centrosome function and ciliogenesis (GO:0034343|GO:0005813) —LEADS_TO→ cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010); cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ retinitis pigmentosa (HP:0000547); CDK5RAP2 (HGNC:29297) —DISRUPTS→ centriole duplication and mitotic spindle assembly (GO:0051004|GO:0007097); centriole duplication and mitotic spindle assembly (GO:0051004|GO:0007097) —LEADS_TO→ cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010); cytoskeletal organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ primary microcephaly (HP:0000252). Mutations in OFD1 disrupt centrosome function and ciliogenesis, leading to cellular dysfunction that impacts cytoskeletal organization and ultimately photoreceptor integrity, causing retinitis pigmentosa. Similarly, mutations in CDK5RAP2 disrupt centriole duplication and mitotic spindle assembly, also impacting cytoskeletal organization, but in the context of neural progenitor cells, leading to primary microcephaly. The shared convergence on cytoskeletal organization and broader cellular processes links these distinct disease modules.
